dedupe_keys.name: redi rating system resilience based earthquake design and downtime assessment arup

description: REDi is a set of prescriptive guidelines from Arup for owners, engineers and architects to implement resilience-based design with objectives beyond code, which the site defines as combining enhanced design, contingency planning and risk verification so that owners can resume operations or provide liveable conditions quickly after a disaster. The guidelines rest on four pillars (operational, building and site resilience, and resilience assessment) and three rating tiers, Platinum, Gold and Silver, each focused on continuity or recovery of core services; the FAQ explains that codes target life safety but do not aim to limit damage or keep function. Coverage: generic, aimed at new buildings. Access: free guidelines download from the REDi website. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): Arup REDi licence (limited worldwide licence for non-commercial and commercial use; no resale). Caveats: written for new design, not existing buildings, and the downtime and loss figures depend on the loss assessment method applied, which carries its own uncertainty. Simulation uses: estimating repair time and functional recovery for building portfolios after earthquakes, and setting resilience targets in recovery models. Related records: FEMA P-58 PACT, Pelicun and the FEMA P-58 fragility database.
